units.title: Unit 12: Past Continuous vs. Past Simple
units.objective: Form and apply the Past Continuous tense (was/were + verb-ing), construct negatives, questions, and short answers, and accurately distinguish background actions (Past Continuous) from interrupting events (Past Simple) using when and while.

lessons.title: Lesson 12.1: Formation of the Past Continuous Tense
lessons.explanation_en: Form the ordinary past continuous with was/were + verb-ing to view an activity as in progress at a past reference time. Use was with I/he/she/it and ordinary singular noun phrases; use were with you/we/they and plural noun phrases. You takes were for one addressee or several. Many final silent-e verbs drop e: write/writing; but see/seeing keeps its vowel letters. Final ie changes to y: lie/lying. One-syllable verbs with one vowel letter representing a short vowel followed by one final consonant letter often double that consonant: run/running, sit/sitting; do not double final w, x or y. Longer verbs depend on stress and sometimes spelling variety. A clock time alone does not force the continuous: the chosen view of the event matters.
lessons.clarification_ar: نصوغ الماضي المستمر من was/were ثم الفعل بصيغة ing لننظر إلى النشاط وهو جارٍ عند وقت ماضٍ. تأخذ you الصيغة were للمفرد والجمع. كثير من الأفعال ذات e الصامتة تحذفها مثل write/writing، لكن see/seeing تحتفظ بحروف العلة، وlie تصبح lying. نضاعف الساكن في أمثلة مثل run/running مع شروط المقطع الواحد وحرف العلة القصير، ولا نضاعف w أوx أوy. الساعة وحدها لا تفرض المستمر؛ المعنى المقصود مهم.
examples: The IT manager was updating the security system yesterday afternoon.
The engineers were reviewing the project plans at 3:00 PM.
She was writing the quarterly report during the morning shift.
common_mistakes: Use was/were before the -ing form for the target continuous construction.
Use was writing, not was write, to describe this activity in progress. Other was + past-form patterns can belong to other constructions, outside this lesson.
Do not drop every final e or double every final consonant without checking the spelling pattern.

lessons.title: Lesson 12.2: Past Continuous Negatives, Questions, and Short Answers
lessons.explanation_en: For a negative, put not after was/were and keep the -ing form: was not/wasn't working, were not/weren't working. For ordinary yes/no questions, invert be and the subject: Were you working? Do not use did/didn't to construct this continuous pattern. Short answers repeat the appropriate auxiliary, not the lexical verb: Yes, I was; No, I wasn't. Yes, I was working is also grammatical, but it is a fuller answer rather than the requested short-answer form. With plural you, a speaker answering for a group can say Yes, we were.
lessons.clarification_ar: للنفي نضع not بعد was/were مع الإبقاء على ing، وللسؤال نقدم was/were على الفاعل. في هذا النمط لا نستخدم did/didn't. الإجابة القصيرة Yes, I was صحيحة، وكذلك الإجابة الكاملة Yes, I was working؛ الفرق في طول الإجابة لا في الصحة النحوية. وقد يجيب متحدث باسم مجموعة بـYes, we were بحسب المقصود.
lessons.form: Negative: Subject + 'wasn't'/'weren't' + Verb-ing | Question: 'Was'/'Were' + Subject + Verb-ing...? | Short Answer: 'Yes, [subject] was/were.' / 'No, [subject] wasn't/weren't.'
examples: The technicians weren't operating the machines at three yesterday.
Were you attending the course at ten yesterday?
Yes, I was. / No, I was not.
Yes, I was attending the course. (A grammatical fuller answer.)
common_mistakes: Use wasn't/weren't + verb-ing for the requested past-continuous negative, rather than didn't + verb-ing.
Do not call a full answer such as Yes, I was working ungrammatical; distinguish it from an auxiliary-only short answer.

lessons.title: Lesson 12.3: Past Continuous vs. Past Simple: Background Action and Interruption
lessons.explanation_en: The past continuous can present an activity in progress as background: I was drafting the report. The past simple can present another event as a whole within that period: the phone rang. This pairing does not prove the background activity stopped, and simple/continuous choices do not depend only on how many minutes an event lasted. Two simple forms or two continuous forms can be grammatical with different viewpoints. These drills explicitly request one background-in-progress form and one whole-event form. Useful event forms here include ring/rang, shut/shut, crash/crashed and occur/occurred; occur doubles r in occurred because its final syllable is stressed.
lessons.clarification_ar: قد يعرض الماضي المستمر نشاطًا وهو جارٍ كخلفية، ويعرض الماضي البسيط حدثًا آخر كواقعة كاملة داخل تلك الفترة. لا يعني ذلك بالضرورة أن النشاط الأول توقف، ولا يعتمد الاختيار على طول الحدث وحده. قد يصح البسيط للفعلين أوالمستمر للفعلين مع اختلاف زاوية العرض. تحدد هذه التدريبات النمط المطلوب صراحة. من الصيغ المستخدمة ring/rang وshut/shut وoccur/occurred.
lessons.form: Background Action: Past Continuous (was/were + verb-ing) | Interrupting Action: Past Simple (verb-ed / irregular past)
examples: I was inspecting the warehouse when the auditor arrived.
The system crashed while the data analyst was backing up the files.
She answered the phone while she was preparing the financial report.
common_mistakes: Do not assume every pair of simultaneous events must use one fixed tense pairing.
Was arriving and arrived can both be grammatical; choose the viewpoint requested by the particular task.
Do not assume a background activity must stop when another event occurs.

lessons.title: Lesson 12.4: Simultaneous Actions with When and While
lessons.explanation_en: While commonly links overlapping situations; when locates one event relative to another. Neither word mechanically selects a tense. While I was reading is common, but While I worked there can describe a past period without a continuous verb. Both when and while can introduce a past continuous background in an appropriate context. To explicitly view two overlapping activities as ongoing, a writer can use the continuous in both clauses: While Mark was checking stock, Sarah was updating the list. A simple form can express a different view; it is not automatically an error. Clause order may change without changing the basic relationship, and a fronted time clause normally takes a comma in edited writing.
lessons.clarification_ar: تربط while غالبًا بين مواقف متداخلة زمنيًا، وتحدد when وقت حدث بالنسبة لآخر، ولا تختار أي منهما الزمن آليًا. يمكن قول While I worked there بالماضي البسيط، وكذلك استخدام when أوwhile مع خلفية بالمستمر حسب السياق. لعرض نشاطين متداخلين وهما جاريان يمكن استخدام المستمر في الجملتين، دون اعتبار كل اختيار آخر خطأ.
lessons.form: 'While' + Past Continuous, Past Continuous (Two simultaneous actions) | 'While' + Past Continuous, Past Simple (Background + Interruption) | 'When' + Past Simple, Past Continuous (Point of time + Background)
examples: While the technicians were repairing the server, the manager was briefing the clients.
While I worked there, I walked to the office every day.
The manager arrived when the employees were discussing the plan.
common_mistakes: Assuming 'while' must strictly be followed by a continuous form in every single context.
Confusing clause order or tense pairing between background and interrupting actions.

questions.prompt: Select the sentence that correctly forms the Past Continuous tense for a plural subject.
options: The accountants was reviewing the audit files at 4:00 PM.
The accountants were reviewing the audit files at 4:00 PM.
The accountants were review the audit files at 4:00 PM.
The accountants did reviewing the audit files at 4:00 PM.
questions.answer: The accountants were reviewing the audit files at 4:00 PM.
accepted_answers: The accountants were reviewing the audit files at 4:00 PM.
questions.explanation: Plural subject ('The accountants') takes 'were' + verb-ing ('were reviewing').

options: The technicians didn't working during the night shift.

questions.prompt: For a question addressed to one person, choose the past-continuous question and matching auxiliary-only affirmative short answer.
options: Was you monitoring the system logs? Yes, I did.
Were you monitoring the system logs? Yes, I was.
Did you monitoring the system logs? Yes, I was.
Were you monitor the system logs? Yes, I monitored.
questions.answer: Were you monitoring the system logs? Yes, I was.
accepted_answers: Were you monitoring the system logs? Yes, I was.
questions.explanation: Were you monitoring...? pairs with Yes, I was when one addressee answers. Yes, I was monitoring would also be grammatical but would be a fuller answer.

questions.prompt: Choose the offered sentence using past continuous for drafting as an activity in progress, and past simple for the single completed call from the supervisor.
options: I was drafting the report when the supervisor called me into his office.
I drafted the report when the supervisor was calling me into his office.
I was drafting the report when the supervisor was calling me into his office.
I draft the report when the supervisor called me into his office.
questions.answer: I was drafting the report when the supervisor called me into his office.
accepted_answers: I was drafting the report when the supervisor called me into his office.
questions.explanation: Was drafting presents the background in progress; called presents the single call as a whole. The other tense pairings can convey other viewpoints, so the request specifies the target forms.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses while and past-continuous forms in both clauses to view both overlapping activities as in progress?
options: While the manager was presenting the slides, the assistant was taking meeting notes.
While the manager presented the slides, the assistant was took meeting notes.
While the manager was present the slides, the assistant was take meeting notes.
While the manager did present the slides, the assistant did take meeting notes.
questions.answer: While the manager was presenting the slides, the assistant was taking meeting notes.
accepted_answers: While the manager was presenting the slides, the assistant was taking meeting notes.
questions.explanation: The first option uses was presenting and was taking. The did present/did take option can be grammatical emphatic simple past, but it does not meet the requested two-continuous-forms pattern.

questions.prompt: Rewrite only was shutting down in the past simple to present the shutdown as a whole event; keep the rest: 'I was checking my emails when the computer was shutting down.'
questions.answer: I was checking my emails when the computer shut down.
accepted_answers: I was checking my emails when the computer shut down.
questions.explanation: Shut down is the requested past-simple whole-event form; shut has the same base and past spelling. Was shutting down can also be grammatical when the shutdown is viewed in progress. This is a controlled viewpoint rewrite, not a claim that the original is always wrong.

writing_tasks.prompt: Write a 60–90-word workplace incident report about yesterday. Include a past-continuous background, a past-simple event during it, two overlapping activities viewed in progress with while, and a negative past-continuous sentence using wasn't/weren't or the uncontracted equivalents. Do not use perfect tenses.
writing_tasks.model_response: Yesterday at three, I was taking notes while my colleague was showing the project slides. The projector suddenly stopped while we were explaining the plan. We weren't expecting a problem because the equipment was new. A technician checked the cable and fixed the loose connection. While he was working, we were answering the client's questions. The presentation resumed ten minutes later.
review_criteria: Use was/were + verb-ing consistently for the intended background-in-progress viewpoint.
Use a past-simple form for the requested whole event without assuming every event must end the background activity.
Include two overlapping activities both viewed in progress with while; do not infer a universal tense rule for while.
Use a past-continuous negative with was not/wasn't or were not/weren't.
Aim for 60–90 words and a coherent incident report. Word count alone does not establish writing quality.
